Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the recap and the summary PDF — very helpful. Quick answers to your questions below and attaching our questionnaire (acme_questionnaire_responses.xlsx) with the initial responses filled where possible.

PII categories in our prompts:
- Patient full name
- Patient ID (internal Acme patient id)
- DOB
- Truncated SSN (last 4 digits) in some workflows
- In rare cases free-text clinical notes with PHI (we can flag these examples)

Deployment preference:
- Short term: Hosted API to iterate quickly; long term: Dedicated or Private for production (regulatory considerations).

Retention/residency questions (high level):
- For Hosted: Do you store the raw prompts and generated outputs? For how long? Where (region) are they stored?
- For Dedicated/Private: Can logging/retention be turned off entirely? Can we enforce US-only residency?

Attached: acme_questionnaire_responses.xlsx (responses + a few follow-up questions inline).

Appreciate a consolidated statement we can share with our InfoSec and procurement teams.

Best,
Amy

Subject: Re: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts/outputs - confirmation and next steps

Hi Amy — thanks for the details and the questionnaire. Below is a concise, artifact-ready summary of Redwood's default hosted behavior and the Dedicated/Private options. I’ve also noted a few items we should confirm internally (cc'ing Marissa and Neha).

SUMMARY (short version for InfoSec/procurement):
- Hosted (Redwood-managed):
  - Prompts and outputs: By default, transient logs that include prompts and generated outputs are retained for 30 days, encrypted at rest and in transit. Data is stored in the region serving the request (we can pin to US regions).
  - Metadata and operational logs: Retained for 90 days for troubleshooting and billing audit purposes.
  - KV cache & ephemeral state: Not persisted to long-term storage; used for active sessions only.
  - Access controls: Data encrypted with customer tenant keys (KMS) and role-based access in our control plane. SOC 2 Type II report available on request.

- Dedicated / Private deployments:
  - Logging/retention controls: Customer-configurable. Logging of prompts/outputs can be disabled entirely; retention windows can be set to meet your policy.
  - Data residency: For Dedicated, we can provision capacity in your chosen cloud region (US-only if required). For Private/on-prem, data never leaves your network unless you opt in.
  - Key management: Option to bring your own key (BYOK) via KMS/HSM integrations for Dedicated/Private.

Other notes / clarifications:
- We do not use customer prompts/outputs for model training.
- Redaction: We provide guidance and tooling to redact or token-mask fields in prompts before storage if you want an additional protection layer.
- SOC2 / artifacts: I can share our SOC 2 Type II and a short security FAQ.

Requested next steps:
1) Rishi: I’ll share a tailored one-page confirmation you can hand to procurement/security (ETA: EOD tomorrow) — please confirm if the 30-day default retention for hosted is acceptable to record in the document.
2) Amy / Brian: Please highlight any required retention windows or residency policies in the questionnaire so we can include explicit statements.
3) Marissa / Neha (internal): Can Security produce SOC2 and the audit artifact links and confirm the BYOK options and exact retention fields?

Quoted for context:
> "For Hosted: Do you store the raw prompts and generated outputs? For how long? Where (region) are they stored?"

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the one-pager and links.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
